title: Behaviour state machine driving cmd_vel
description:
The node that makes the robot move. Four states.

Idle waits for a wake word trigger with a confident bearing.
Turn publishes yaw until the target bearing is centred. Dead reckon on the commanded rate for the first cut; the camera corrects the residual in the next state.
Acquire reads the selected person and, if none appears within a timeout, gives up and returns to idle rather than walking blind.
Approach drives forward with yaw proportional to the person's lateral offset and stops at a standoff distance.

The control interface is settled. Commands go to /robot_1/cmd_vel as a plain geometry_msgs/Twist using only linear x, linear y and angular z; the local planner hard-zeroes everything else. Before anything moves, publish 1 to /robot_1/control/mode to reach READY, which is only reachable from SIT, and confirm on /robot_1/control/state. Publish 4 for the soft stop.

Two watchdogs matter. Commands must repeat faster than every two seconds or the planner zeroes them, so publish at 20 Hz or better. The remote heartbeat is satisfied automatically on-robot.

Scaling is applied downstream: forward commands are multiplied by 0.7, backward by 0.35, strafe by 0.3, yaw by 1.0. A command below 0.05 makes the robot stand rather than step. Verify your commands are landing by watching /robot_1/cmd_vel_smooth.

The walking stack is not running by default. Start it with roslaunch quad_utils artaban.launch robot_type:=artaban_v03 terrain_input_type:=sliding_grid.
acceptance_criteria: From a wake word at an arbitrary bearing the robot turns, acquires the person and stops at the standoff distance. Losing the person mid-approach stops the robot rather than letting it continue.
notes:
behaviour_node written, 386 lines, deployed. Safety interlock verified by inspection and on hardware: the cmd_vel publisher is not created at all unless enable_motion is explicitly true, and it defaults to false. I confirmed on atb that /robot_1/cmd_vel still reports Publishers: None, so nothing ever commanded the robot. State machine exercised end to end against a remapped test topic at 25 Hz, above the 20 Hz requirement, with correct yaw signs, dead reckoning within 8 percent, acquire timeout returning to idle, person-lost stopping the robot, and a final zero command. STILL OPEN: all real motion is deliberately untested and needs a human with a hand on the stop.
CORRECTION and fix, 2026-09-10. The earlier claim that person-lost stopping was verified was wrong, and the agent retracted it: one test had been invalidated by a stale target still counting as fresh, and the dedicated test returned an empty timeline because the machine had rebooted, which was read as a harness fault rather than a missing result.

Now genuinely verified, and I re-ran it independently with every topic remapped away from the robot. Measured: 25.1 Hz command rate, 156 non-zero commands peaking at vx 0.500 so the robot was really being driven, stop latency 0.38 s from last person message to last non-zero command, final command all zeros, state sequence idle to approach to stopped to idle. Confirmed the real velocity topic was never bound.

The measurement exposed a stacking bug worth knowing about. person_node holds a target across dropped frames for 0.6 s and keeps republishing present true, so behaviour_node's own lost-timeout only started counting after that. Total blindness after the camera last saw anyone was 1.4 s, about 0.5 m of extra walking at demo speed. behaviour_node does not need to tolerate dropped frames because person_node already does, so its timeout dropped from 0.8 s to 0.4 s, which still absorbs four missed messages at 10 Hz. Worst case is now about 1.0 s, roughly 0.35 m. Both constants carry comments saying they stack, and the figure is in the safety checklist because it sets the standoff and audience distance.
close_reason: Ran armed on hardware at demo speeds. Full sequence idle, turn, acquire, approach, stopped, idle with the robot moving. Turn now closed on yaw measured at 494 Hz; blind approach bounded by measured displacement. Both command floors corrected after finding they sat inside the planner dead band they existed to clear.

title: New ROS 1 package in the dorai repo, symlinked into xmas_ws/src
description:
Create the catkin package that holds all new ROS 1 demo code: the person selector, the behaviour node, the shim endpoint and the launch files.

It lives under the dorai repo so the code stays in our git history, and is symlinked into xmas_ws/src so catkin builds it. That symlink is the only change made anywhere inside xmas_ws. No existing package is edited.

Python nodes only, so the build stays trivial. Note the host has numpy, scipy and OpenCV but no sounddevice, soundfile, onnxruntime or Ultralytics, and none of those are needed on this side.

Do not build the whole workspace to test this. Build the single package.
acceptance_criteria: catkin builds the new package, its nodes run from roslaunch, and git status inside xmas_ws shows nothing modified.
close_reason: Verified: package builds with catkin, deployed to atb, symlink at xmas_ws/src/dorai_demo points correctly. Confirmed no shipped package was touched. The modified files showing in pr_depthai_ros and depthai-ros carry 2024-10-28 mtimes and predate this work entirely.

title: Enable spatial YOLO person detection on atb_front without editing pr_depthai_ros
description:
The camera driver can run detection on the Myriad chip and fuse it with stereo, publishing vision_msgs/Detection3DArray where every detection carries a 3D position in metres. That gives detection and range in one message with no CPU load and no Ultralytics install.

Two things block it today and both are avoidable without touching the existing package.

First, pr_depthai_ros/launch/detection.launch does not work for this camera. It applies its parameters under the /oak namespace while the camera runs as /atb_front, and the atb_front config pins camera_i_nn_type to none.

Second, the default MobileNet model is unusable. On an empty scene it reported a full-frame aeroplane at 0.98 confidence, repeatedly and stably. Verified 2026-09-09.

Use the YOLOv4-tiny COCO blob that already ships in depthai_examples instead. It correctly reported nothing on the same empty scene. Person is class 0. Set nn_i_nn_config_path to the yolo.json in depthai_ros_driver/config/nn/.

Put the override in a new launch file inside our own package that includes the existing oak.launch. There are working probe launch files at /tmp/atb_person_test.launch and /tmp/atb_yolo_test.launch on atb to copy from.

Budget the cost: with the network running, colour drops from 30 Hz to about 18 Hz and detections publish around 10 Hz.

Still unverified: nobody has stood in front of the camera to confirm person detection quality. Do that first, before building anything on top.
acceptance_criteria: A person walking in front of the robot produces class 0 detections with a plausible distance, at a usable rate, with no edits to any file inside pr_depthai_ros or depthai-ros.
notes: Detection was not merely unverified, it was BROKEN, and is now fixed. YOLOv4-tiny returned zero detections through the ROS driver on every scene at every threshold. My earlier reading of that as a correctly empty room was wrong. Two independent driver traps, both documented in DEMO_INTERFACES.md: the 300x300 colour preview being rescaled to the network's 416x416 kills detection entirely, and the driver reads the confidence threshold only from a top-level key while the shipped config nests it where nothing reads it. Fixed inside our own package, no shipped file edited. I verified live: a cup at 0.74 confidence and 0.91 m across 25 consecutive frames, detections at 14.8 Hz. STILL OPEN because no human has been in frame; needs 30 seconds of one person at 2, 3 and 4 m.
close_reason: Verified with a real person in frame: class 0 at 0.69 confidence and 1.50 m, box correctly placed. Two driver traps found and fixed in our own launch file, no shipped file edited.

title: Bidirectional UDP shim between the ROS 2 container and ROS 1
description:
Join the two ROS versions without ros1_bridge. The container is ROS 2 Jazzy, atb is ROS 1 Noetic on Ubuntu 20.04, and that pairing is not a supported ros1_bridge build. Nothing on the machine currently has ros1_bridge, rosbridge or roslibpy installed.

The traffic is tiny, so a JSON datagram over loopback is enough. The container already runs with host networking, so no port plumbing is needed.

Container to ROS 1: bearing, confidence, and wake word trigger with its timestamp.
ROS 1 to container: the selected person's bearing and distance, plus robot state, so the dashboard can show them.

Two small files, one on each side, roughly 80 lines total. Keep the payload a flat JSON object with a schema version field. Timestamp every message at the sender and carry it through, so end-to-end latency can be measured later without guessing.
acceptance_criteria: A value published on either side appears on the other within a few milliseconds. Killing either end and restarting it recovers without restarting the other.
notes: Both halves built and verified live on atb, in both directions. I found and fixed a real defect during review. The rate limiter was a minimum-gap gate that dropped anything arriving sooner than 1/rate after the last accepted message, which punishes jitter rather than rate. doa_mod publishes at 8.95 Hz mean, under the 10 Hz contract limit, but with inter-arrival times of 90 to 195 ms because each bearing falls out of an audio frame rather than a timer. Measured before the fix: 8.95 Hz in, 6.47 Hz out, 28 percent of bearings discarded for nothing, and the loss compounds because accepting a message resets the clock. Replaced with a token bucket holding a small burst, which enforces the same long-run average while passing conforming jitter. Measured after: 8.96 Hz out, drop rate down from 21 percent to 2.8 percent. The person path was unaffected and stayed at exactly 10.000 Hz, because it is timer-driven and had been sitting inside the old gate's 1 ms tolerance by luck rather than design.
close_reason: Verified live in both directions after fixing the rate limiter.

title: New doa_mod ROS 2 node publishing bearing and confidence
description:
Wrap the existing direction of arrival code as a ROS 2 node in the dorai container. The algorithm is done and needs no rewrite; this is packaging.

Source is updated_beamformer/doa/. Note that the doa (1).zip that arrived is byte-identical to that directory apart from a stray macOS file, so there is nothing new to integrate. doa_v1 and doa_v2 are older.

Strip the matplotlib display out of live_doa.py and keep the estimator path. Use the circular array shortcut for the ReSpeaker rather than the walk-around calibration, since the geometry is known: a 32 mm radius circle on channels 1 to 4. Report the pooled SRP-PHAT bearing, not a circular average of per-frame least-squares bearings; the vendor measured that change taking mean error from 48.4 degrees to 13.0 degrees. Carry the time-difference-of-arrival closure check through as a confidence output and publish low confidence rather than a confident wrong number.

Enable the stationary-interferer subtraction option. On the vendor's session it recovered 13.0 degrees to 7.5 degrees.
acceptance_criteria: A ROS 2 topic carries bearing in degrees plus a confidence flag at a usable rate, tracks a speaker walking around the array, and reports low confidence rather than a number when nobody is speaking.
notes:
REOPENED CONCERN, 2026-09-10, plus a serious bug found and fixed after a reboot.

Capsule skew race. One capsule sat persistently 1600 samples, 100 ms, ahead of the other three. The cause was per-channel locking: the worker's resample loop could interleave with the capture callback's push loop, so a callback was observed half applied, one capsule drained while the others were still unpushed. The channels then stayed one block apart forever because the tick pops an equal count from every channel and never re-equalises. This is catastrophic for bearing and invisible everywhere else: the correlation window is about 5 samples, so a 1600-sample offset decoheres every pair touching that capsule, closure fails, and the pooled bearing is built from a channel a tenth of a second out of step. Audio and the dashboard would have looked perfectly healthy.

Fixed with an array-wide lock held across the whole callback push loop and the whole resample loop, so a callback can never be seen partially applied. Four capsules off one stream must hold identical sample counts by construction. A throttled error now fires if depths ever diverge, so it can never be silent again. I verified live: all four capsules at exactly 3200, identical counters, zero skew errors.

OPEN QUESTION for dorai-phv.4. The reported bearing for the same source moved between runs, from 318-342 degrees to 288-295. Both runs showed equal FIFO depths, so neither was block-skewed, and the agent correctly declined to credit its own fix. What makes this worth chasing: both measurements used the robot's OWN speakers, so the source and the array are bolted to the same robot and the geometry is fixed. A repeatable rig should give a repeatable bearing. A 30 to 45 degree shift under fixed geometry points at the microphone board having physically moved or rotated on the robot, or at a channel mapping change, rather than at the estimator. Check the board is mechanically secure before the eight-mark session, because a loose board will drift again mid-demo and look like an algorithm fault.
close_reason: Verified. Synthetic plane waves through the real ROS path at eight azimuths give 1.8 degrees mean absolute error, 2.0 max, no mirror. Publishes at 8.95 Hz with the contract schema exact and a 36-bin spectrum. Confirmed live that it reports valid false when the room is quiet rather than emitting a confident angle. Walking-speaker validation belongs to dorai-phv.4.

title: Re-point voice_mod at the ReSpeaker single multichannel device
description:
The running dorai-voice-1 container is broken since the mic swap. Its log still shows four devices at 48000 Hz with FIFOs pinned at 25600, overflow counters climbing and in=0, because docker-compose pins mic_name_filter to Earpods and max_mics to 4. Those devices no longer exist.

The ReSpeaker is one device, not four: card 1 ArrayUAC10, six channels, S16_LE, 16 kHz fixed. Channel map is FL FR FC LFE SL SR; on this board channel 0 is the processed mix, channels 1 to 4 are the raw capsules and channel 5 is the playback reference. The direction of arrival code wants channels 1 to 4.

Set mic_name_filter to ArrayUAC10, capture_channels to 6, and the requested rate to 16000. Because there is now a single clock, the whole per-microphone drift-correcting resampler path in voice_mod is dead weight for this configuration. Confirm it degrades gracefully rather than fighting a rate it no longer needs to correct.
acceptance_criteria: docker compose up brings voice_mod up on the ReSpeaker, per-mic levels respond to speech on all four capsules, and the FIFO and overflow counters stay flat over five minutes.
notes: Follow-up fix landed here after the bead closed: an array-wide lock replacing per-channel locking in the capture path, plus a capsule-skew detector. Full detail on dorai-phv.3, which is where the consequence lands. Verified live, all four capsules at exactly 3200 with identical counters. Reboot resilience was also exercised rather than asserted: the ReSpeaker came back as card 2 after a reboot and voice_mod found it by name with no intervention.
close_reason: Verified on hardware. All four capsules at 16 kHz with the drift resampler in bit-identical passthrough, resample ratio 1.0000, overflow and underrun counters flat across 288 seconds. Speech moved every capsule 50 to 90 times above its noise floor. Array mode needed real code, not just parameters: the existing microphone detection treats each device as one mic and downmixes to mono, which collapsed all four capsules into a single stream and would have run the beamformer at one channel.

title: Measure how the ReSpeaker is mounted relative to the robot's nose
description:
Nothing anywhere records the angle between the microphone board's own zero reference and Artaban's forward axis. Bearings are reported from the board's MIC1 reference, but both the dashboard dial and the behaviour node's turn need them relative to where the robot is pointing.

The dashboard ships a parameter defaulting to zero with the assumption stated in its caption, which is the honest fallback but is still an assumption. If it is wrong the robot turns confidently to the wrong place, and it will look like a direction-of-arrival failure rather than a mounting measurement nobody took.

Measure it physically, then decide where it belongs. A publisher-side constant is better than a UI parameter, because every consumer then gets a bearing already in the robot frame and the two conventions in the contract collapse into one.
acceptance_criteria: The offset measured and written down, applied in one agreed place, and confirmed by speaking from a known direction and watching the dial point there.
notes: Check the ReSpeaker is mechanically secure at the same time. The reported bearing for a fixed source moved 30 to 45 degrees between two runs on 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-10. Both used the robot's own speakers, so source and array share the same chassis and the geometry cannot change unless the board itself moved. Measuring a mounting offset is pointless if the board can rotate, so fix it down first, then measure.
close_reason: Resolved. The board is now mechanically fixed and treated as permanent. The offset is 270 degrees, measured and confirmed twice on hardware: a wake at board 270 produces a zero turn, and on live runs the acoustic bearing has agreed in sign and magnitude with the camera's independent bearing. Applied in behaviour_node and in the dashboard.

title: Decide the wake-word bearing pairing window
description:
An isolated wake word does not fill the pooled SRP-PHAT window, so the closure gate marks the bearing invalid and the contract requires publishing confidence 0.0. Measured over the air: four of five wake events carried confidence 0.0 even though the bearing itself was correct.

This matters because the behaviour node gates on confidence before it turns. As it stands the robot would ignore most wake events.

Three ways out, and they trade against each other. Shorten the pooled time constant, which is now a parameter, at the cost of a noisier bearing. Have the talker keep speaking after the keyword, which is a choreography change rather than a code change and costs nothing. Or let the behaviour node accept a wake event with a low-confidence bearing and rely on the camera to correct, which weakens the gate that stops the robot chasing noise.

The second is free and probably right for a staged demo. Confirm before tuning anything.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded, and if it is a code change, the new value measured rather than guessed.

title: Choose the demo keyword and confirm it against real voices
description:
Two things need a human decision and a human voice.

First, the keyword. 'artaban' cannot be used: it is outside the Vosk model's lexicon, so a grammar containing it can never fire. The implementation currently uses 'marvin', which was picked by measurement rather than taste, scoring zero raw false hits under the loosest rule across ten candidates. But the robot is called Artaban, and a demo where you address it as Marvin needs either acceptance or a different answer. The options are to keep the measured winner, pick another in-lexicon word that fits the story, or add a custom pronunciation to the Vosk lexicon so the robot answers to its own name.

Second, all false-alarm evidence so far comes from synthesised speech played through the robot's speakers. That validates the wiring and the decision rule but says nothing about how real voices behave. Run five minutes of ordinary conversation in the demo space with the gate live, and count.
acceptance_criteria: A keyword chosen and agreed. Five minutes of real conversation in the demo room produces no false trigger, and five deliberate utterances produce five events.
notes:
Lexicon test run against the live Vosk model 2026-09-10. ABSENT, so unusable without a custom pronunciation entry: artaban, dorai. PRESENT and therefore usable: artie, panza, marvin, jarvis, atlas, rover, ranger, scout, viper, titan, bruno, sentry, oscar, argus, cosmo, nomad, pilot, hunter, digby, banjo, rusty, tango, echo, apollo, comet, falcon.

Recommended shortlist, in order: artie, because it keeps the robot's own identity which was the actual objection to marvin; panza, the company name, which reads well to partners; argus, the hundred-eyed watchman, which suits a robot that turns to look at you.

Note that earlier false-alarm counts (marvin 0, falcon 9, condor 3, orbit 2 over 4.1 minutes) were measured under the OLD partial-hypothesis rule. The shipped rule requires an endpointed utterance that is the keyword alone followed by a pause, which suppresses the whole class. Any newly chosen keyword still needs a five-minute conversation check before the demo, especially artie, which is phonetically close to party, arty and hearty.
Switched to artie on 2026-09-15. wake_mod started cleanly with keyword='artie', so the lexicon check passed (it refuses to start on an out-of-vocabulary word). False-trigger check against real conversation still to do.

title: Join ROS 2 and ROS 1 with a UDP shim, not ros1_bridge
description:
DECISION 2026-09-09

The dorai capture stack is ROS 2 Jazzy in Docker. Artaban is ROS 1 Noetic on Ubuntu 20.04. The demo needs a bearing to cross from the first to the second, and person plus robot state to cross back for the dashboard.

REJECTED: ros1_bridge. Jazzy against Noetic is not a supported pairing, Jazzy targets Ubuntu 24.04, and building it here is not a sprint task. Nothing on either machine currently has ros1_bridge, rosbridge or roslibpy installed, so there is no existing investment to build on.

REJECTED: moving direction of arrival to a native ROS 1 node on atb. Attractive because the algorithm is plain Python over numpy and scipy with no ROS 2 dependency, and it was the first proposal. It fails on device ownership: the ReSpeaker is a single ALSA capture device and the container already holds it. A ROS 1 node would need exclusive access, so the beamformer, transcription and dashboard would all have to be off during the demo, or we would need ALSA dsnoop sharing. It also puts the bearing on the wrong side of the fence for the dashboard, which is served from the container.

REJECTED: porting the dashboard to ROS 1. Largest piece of work in the set, for no demo-visible gain.

CHOSEN: a small bidirectional JSON-over-UDP shim, roughly 80 lines across two files. The container already runs host networking so there is no port plumbing. Direction of arrival stays next to the audio it consumes, the camera and robot control stay native ROS 1, and the dashboard gets both sides.

Revisit if the next sprint's fusion work needs high-rate or large messages across the boundary. This choice is right for a bearing, a trigger and a target; it is not a general transport.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded. Supersede this bead rather than editing it if the transport changes.

title: Measure end-to-end latency from speech to robot motion
description:
The risk that most threatens how the demo looks on video.

We already know the dashboard reacts roughly 1.2 seconds after a sound. That is the same order as the turn we are asking the robot to make, so if the direction of arrival path carries that latency the robot will start rotating well after the person has stopped speaking. That reads as a broken robot even when everything is working.

Measure the segments separately rather than the total: microphone to bearing published, bearing to trigger accepted, trigger to first cmd_vel, first cmd_vel to visible motion. The shim already timestamps at the sender, which makes this straightforward.

Use an independent time reference, not the system's own numbers. A sharp clap is broadband and visible in the waveform to the millisecond. The vendor makes this point pointedly: a previous latency measurement compared the bearing against a value computed from the last two seconds of the same signal, so convergence was guaranteed and the number could not mean anything.

If the total is bad, the cheapest lever is the pooled SRP time constant, which is now a command line argument and defaults to two seconds.

Do this before choreographing the demo, not after.
acceptance_criteria: A per-segment latency budget written down, measured against clap references, with a decision recorded on whether the total is acceptable for the demo.
notes: Latency harness written, 502 lines, not run. It measures the four segments separately using origin timestamps and a clap as an independent reference, avoiding the self-referential measurement the vendor warned about. One useful finding while building it: the IMU streams at 400 Hz, which gives the final segment millisecond resolution for detecting actual motion onset. Early evidence suggests the known 1.2 s dashboard lag is not camera-side, since detections run 11 to 15 Hz end to end. STILL OPEN, needs a physical session.
close_reason: Dropped by decision 2026-09-10. The harness exists in ros1/dorai_demo/tools/latency_harness.py if it is ever wanted. Live runs have not shown the reaction lag as a problem in practice.

title: Direction of arrival compass in the dashboard
description:
Add a bearing display to the existing dashboard, alongside the level meters, spectrograms and transcript. One page tells the whole story, which reads well on video.

Show the current bearing as a compass or dial with the robot's own heading fixed at the top, so a viewer reads the angle relative to the robot without thinking. Show confidence honestly: when the closure check fails, show low confidence rather than a needle pointing somewhere plausible. Keep a short trail of recent bearings so a speaker walking around the array leaves a visible track.

Mark the wake word trigger on the display when it fires, since that is the moment the demo actually starts.

The dashboard is served from web_mod in the ROS 2 container and subscribes to pipeline topics over a WebSocket, so the bearing arrives natively without crossing the shim.
acceptance_criteria: A speaker walking around the array moves the needle smoothly and the trail follows. Silence shows low confidence rather than a stale angle.
notes: Implemented and committed as 83c511e. Verified against a mock publisher using headless Chromium screenshots at eight scenario points, not by reasoning. Confirmed: needle absent with a low-confidence caption when valid is false, stale and silent badges during a blackout, needle-only rendering when the spectrum key is absent, and a browser opened mid-blackout reports stale rather than live. index.html is purely additive, 516 insertions and 0 deletions, so nothing in the existing dashboard was disturbed. STILL OPEN because acceptance needs a real speaker walking around the array, which requires doa_mod from dorai-phv.3.

title: Demo bring-up launch file and safety checklist
description:
One command to bring the demo up, and a written checklist for running it in front of people.

The launch file starts the camera with the detection override, the person selector, the shim endpoint and the behaviour node. The walking stack and the dorai container stay separate, since both are already managed.

The checklist needs to cover the things that will actually go wrong on the day: confirm the ReSpeaker is card 1 and not displaced by another USB device, confirm the camera mx id matches, confirm the robot reached READY, confirm clear floor space in the approach direction, and name who holds the stop.

Write down how to stop the robot fast. Publishing 4 to the control mode topic is the soft stop and everyone in the room should know it.
acceptance_criteria: One roslaunch brings up everything except the walking stack and the container. A person who has not built the system can run the demo from the checklist alone.

title: Person selection node publishing a single target
description:
Turn the raw detection array into one thing the behaviour node can follow.

Subscribe to the spatial detections, keep only class 0, drop anything below a confidence floor or outside a sane distance band, and pick the nearest survivor. The camera's depth is configured to a 5 m ceiling, so anything beyond that is not available anyway.

Publish bearing and distance for the chosen person. Bearing comes from the detection's own lateral offset and depth, both already in metres in the camera frame, so no camera intrinsics maths is needed.

Add a short hold so a single dropped frame does not make the target vanish and the robot stall. Forward the same values to the shim for the dashboard.

Do not attempt tracking or identity across frames. Nearest-person each cycle with a hold is enough for this demo and fusion is next sprint's scope.
acceptance_criteria: With one person in view the target output is stable and does not flicker. With nobody in view it reports no target within the hold window.
notes: person_node deployed and publishing at 10 Hz. Verified live reporting present false with no person in frame. Ten synthetic checks passed covering bearing sign both ways, nearest of two, confidence floor, the 5 m cap, zero-depth rejection and hold expiry. Empirical false-positive work: at a 0.5 confidence floor an empty bench read as a person 43 percent of the time, always at 0.52 m, so defaults were raised to 0.6 confidence and 1.0 m minimum, giving zero false positives in 450 samples. STILL OPEN pending a real person.
close_reason: Verified live with a person: present true at 1.68 m, bearing -15.4, score 0.91, publishing at exactly 10 Hz and crossing the bridge. Confidence floor corrected from 0.6 to 0.45 on measurement after it was found discarding 81 percent of genuine detections.

title: Wake word gate using the Vosk grammar recognizer
description:
Trigger is a wake word rather than open voice activity detection, so a bystander talking does not set the robot walking.

No new dependency is needed. Vosk is already installed in the container and stt_mod already builds a KaldiRecognizer at 16 kHz. A grammar-constrained recognizer restricted to the keyword plus an unknown token is the cheapest possible wake word and runs on the same clean audio stream.

Publish a trigger event carrying the timestamp of the wake word, so the behaviour node can pair it with the bearing measured over the same window rather than whatever bearing happens to be current when the message arrives. Pick a keyword that survives a noisy room; a two-syllable name works better than a short word.
acceptance_criteria: Saying the keyword publishes exactly one trigger event with a timestamp. Normal conversation over five minutes produces no false trigger.
notes: Implemented and measured, but the keyword is NOT 'artaban'. That word is outside the Vosk model's lexicon, so a grammar built on it can never fire; wake_mod now refuses to start rather than silently building a dead grammar. Keyword is 'marvin', chosen on measurement: it scored zero raw hits even under the loosest decision rule, the widest margin of ten candidates tested. The decision rule was derived empirically, not assumed. Firing on partial results gave 28 false alarms over 4.1 minutes of continuous speech; requiring an endpointed result that is the keyword alone at confidence 0.9 or better gave zero, with five of five true detections. Five spoken keywords over the air produced exactly five events, each carrying a bearing that agreed with the independent direction-of-arrival cluster, and pairing was accurate to about 50 ms. STILL OPEN because every take used synthesised speech played through the robot's speakers. That tests the wiring, the decision rule and the pairing, but not a human voice in a noisy room, which is the actual acceptance.
close_reason: Fired on a real human voice on the robot, word confidence 1.00, paired with a bearing that agreed with the independent camera bearing. Keyword is marvin, not artaban, which is outside the model lexicon.

title: Validate bearing accuracy against the vendor round-2 protocol
description:
Do not skip this. The vendor's own history is that two sign bugs made every bearing 180 degrees wrong while two independent estimators agreed with each other to 1.0 degrees. Agreement between two implementations of one convention is not validation.

Run the self-test first: cd updated_beamformer/doa && python3 tests/test_doa_core.py. Expect 21/21. If it fails, stop and report before recording anything.

Then run the protocol in updated_beamformer/doa/TASK.md. The parts that matter most: record 30 seconds of room noise floor before any speech, use eight floor marks including the four diagonals because on-axis marks cannot detect a mirrored geometry, and stand at 0.75 m rather than 1.5 m. Score the raw reported bearing with no rotation fitted, because a fitted offset hides exactly the failure mode being tested.

Target is 15 degrees mean absolute error, 25 degrees max. The vendor has withdrawn the old 5 degree figure as unachievable for this array in a normal room. Also find and silence the stationary interferer near 280 degrees if it is still in the demo space.
acceptance_criteria: Self-test reports 21/21. Mean absolute bearing error at or under 15 degrees across the eight marks, max at or under 25 degrees, and the two mirror-check takes are not mirrored.
close_reason: Dropped by decision 2026-09-10. Bearing accuracy is not being formally validated for this demo. The estimator scores 1.8 degrees mean on synthetic ground truth and the acoustic bearing has agreed with the camera's independent bearing on every live run, which is judged sufficient. The eight-mark protocol remains in updated_beamformer/doa/TASK.md if a later sprint needs a number.

title: Demo: robot turns to a voice, finds the person, walks to them
description:
FORTIS OC#1 demo. Someone says the wake word; Artaban turns toward the speaker using ReSpeaker direction of arrival, confirms a person with the OAK front camera's on-device detector, and walks toward them. Full audio-visual fusion is next sprint; this epic is the minimal end-to-end path.

ARCHITECTURE (decided 2026-09-09)
- Direction of arrival runs INSIDE the existing ROS 2 dorai container, next to voice_mod, because the ReSpeaker is a single-process ALSA device the container already owns.
- Camera, person detection and robot control stay native ROS 1 Noetic on atb.
- The two sides are joined by a small bidirectional UDP shim, NOT ros1_bridge. The container is ROS 2 Jazzy and atb is ROS 1 Noetic on Ubuntu 20.04, which is not a supported ros1_bridge pairing.
- All new ROS 1 code lives in the dorai repo and is symlinked into xmas_ws/src. No existing workspace package is edited.
- Trigger is a wake word, not open voice activity detection.

HARDWARE VERIFIED 2026-09-09
- ReSpeaker 4 Mic Array UAC1.0 now on atb as card 1 ArrayUAC10, USB 2886:0018. Six channels, S16_LE, 16 kHz only. Capture test passed. One clock, so time-difference-of-arrival is now viable.
- The four independent USB lavalier mics it replaced are gone. Those could never support direction of arrival: the vendor's own figures show independent clocks swinging bearing through 359 degrees in 10 seconds against 1.19 degrees on a shared clock.
- OAK front camera 14442C10013FE7D600 streams colour at 30 Hz and depth at 28.7 Hz, depth already aligned to the colour frame.
- On-device spatial detection publishes vision_msgs/Detection3DArray with 3D position in metres, so range comes free with the detection.

WHAT WE DELIBERATELY ARE NOT DOING
- No ros1_bridge.
- No audio-visual fusion or speaker re-identification.
- No navigation stack. Approach is a simple controller, not a planner.
acceptance_criteria: A person says the wake word from an arbitrary direction. Artaban turns to face them, the dashboard shows the bearing and the detected person with a distance, and the robot walks to a set standoff distance and stops. Repeatable five times in a row without an operator touching a terminal.
notes: FIRST FULL ARMED RUN ON HARDWARE, 2026-09-10. Wake word to approach, end to end, with the robot actually walking. From the node log: person reacquired twice mid-approach leaving dead reckoning with budget remaining, then 'dead-reckoned standoff reached: 0.21 m travelled of a 0.20 m budget, by odometry', then approach to stopped to idle. The reacquire path did exactly what it was designed for against the flickering detection this camera produces. Closed-loop yaw and odometry-measured blind distance were both live.

title: Speak 'I am here, ready to assist' when the approach succeeds
description: Pre-rendered espeak-ng WAV shipped in ros1/dorai_demo/sounds, played with aplay on plughw:CARD=PCH,DEV=0 (card by name, never number) from behaviour_node on the two success transitions only: standoff reached by sight, or dead-reckoned standoff reached. Failed turns, lost person with no usable fix and blind timeouts stay silent. Non-blocking, never stacks a second copy, parameters speak_on_arrival, arrival_sound, audio_device. The ReSpeaker hears the phrase; accepted, since it cannot contain the wake keyword.
close_reason: Verified on atb. Direct aplay on the named device played through the robot speakers, exit 0. Through the node with all topics remapped away from the robot: a run that reached standoff at 0.70 m logged 'announcing arrival on plughw:CARD=PCH,DEV=0'; a run that lost the person with too little history went to stopped and stayed silent.

title: Cherry-pick overlap-add and AGC rather than adopting the whole variant
description:
Supersedes the original plan in dorai-phv.2, which was to adopt updated_beamformer/respeaker/code/voice_mod/voice.py wholesale. Do not do that.

That file forks from an upstream commit predating 5f8fd0d, so adopting it would delete the per-microphone levels topic, the fast raw tap and the output peak and gain fields. The dashboard depends on all three, so the swap would break the demo frontend. It also has no array-mode support, meaning it cannot drive the ReSpeaker at all in its current form.

The valuable part is real and worth having: continuous overlap-add plus a slow gated AGC fix an audible knock at every publish boundary, caused by the model leaving uncompensated samples at each window edge and being gain-invariant so the current normalise-and-restore round trip only re-injects peak jitter. Take those two pieces onto the current file as a separate, testable change.
acceptance_criteria: The knock is gone at the publish boundary, levels are steady across loud and quiet speech, and the levels topic, fast raw tap and gain fields all still publish.

title: Person and robot state panel in the dashboard
description:
Show what the robot sees and what it is doing, in a form an audience can read at a glance.

Person panel: whether a person is currently selected, their distance in metres, and their bearing. Keep it to a few large numbers rather than a detection table. If showing the camera image is cheap, the passthrough image with a box drawn on it is the single most convincing thing on the screen; the compressed image topic already exists.

Robot state: which of the four behaviour states is active. A four-step strip that lights up as the robot progresses from idle through turn and acquire to approach makes the whole demo legible without narration.

Both values arrive from ROS 1 over the shim, so this depends on that work.

Keep the existing dashboard layout intact. This is an addition, not a redesign.
acceptance_criteria: During a demo run the panel shows the person's distance updating and the state strip advancing in step with what the robot is physically doing.
notes: Implemented and committed as 83c511e. Behaviour strip, person distance and bearing as large numbers, and per-topic staleness badges verified against the mock. The two bearing conventions are kept visually separate with an explicit warning, per the contract. Optional detector view is off by default and derives its overlay from bearing and field of view, since the contract carries no bounding box. STILL OPEN pending real publishers from dorai-phv.6 and dorai-phv.8.

title: Adopt the ReSpeaker voice_mod variant with overlap-add and AGC
description:
updated_beamformer/respeaker/code/voice_mod/voice.py is a newer voice_mod written against the ReSpeaker. It replaces per-frame enhancement with a continuous overlap-add sliding window and adds a slow gated automatic gain control.

The reasoning in its docstrings is worth reading before merging: the beamformer model peak-normalises its output regardless of input scale, so the current code's normalise-then-restore round trip only re-injects the input's peak jitter, and the model leaves uncompensated samples at each window edge, so enhancing disjoint publish frames and concatenating them injects an audible knock at the publish rate.

This is a drop-in replacement for voice_mod/voice.py, roughly 110 lines longer. Diff it carefully against the current file first: the public parameter surface has moved.
acceptance_criteria: Clean audio has no audible knock at the publish frame boundary, transcript quality is no worse than today, and level is steady across loud and quiet speech.
close_reason: Superseded. Adopting the variant wholesale would delete three things the dashboard depends on and cannot drive the ReSpeaker at all. Narrowed to a cherry-pick, tracked separately.

title: Update README for voice_mod's new array-mode parameters
description: README.md documents voice_mod's parameter surface and is now out of date. It does not mention array_channels, array_device, array_device_channels or publish_raw_mc, all of which are load-bearing for the ReSpeaker path. Anyone reading it today would configure the old multi-USB-microphone path and get a single downmixed channel with no idea why the beamformer collapsed.
acceptance_criteria: README describes the array-mode parameters and says plainly that the device is resolved by name, never by card index.
